subject: Recap & capacity proposal: Lighthouse POC (next steps + sizing)
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-19T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & capacity proposal: Lighthouse POC (next steps + sizing)

Hi Alyssa — great to meet you and the Lighthouse team earlier. Short recap from our discovery and a proposed capacity/eval approach so we can agree on next steps.

Goals / success criteria (suggested):
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency <= 120ms; end-to-end response <= 3s for short prompts, <= 8s for long generative flows.
- Throughput: support peak of ~18 concurrent RPS for API traffic pattern during simulated load.
- Quality: responses meet your internal quality rubric (we'll use your sample prompt set and measure pass rate >= 85%).
- Cost: benchmark tokens/cost under the POC and report unit economics for 100k tokens/day.

Evaluation plan (7–10 day POC, split phases):
1) Smoke (days 1–2): integration, auth, sample prompts, confirm correctness and data routing.
2) Load + stability (days 3–7): synthetic traffic spike tests (match your peak concurrency), KV/prefix caching validation, and model variant A/B to compare quality/cost tradeoffs.

Capacity recommendation (initial):
- Reserved baseline: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (for stable concurrency + KV cache residency).
- Autoscaling: policy to add GPUs in increments of 2 up to 8 GPUs for sustained bursts. Cooldown: 3 minutes; burst window tolerance: 30–45 minutes.
- Expected burst behavior: short spikes (<= 10 minutes) handled by queueing + batching; sustained high load triggers autoscale.

Ownership / roles:
- Redwood: Vivek (sales lead), Laura (SE lead) — Laura will run the sizing tests and coordinate model configs. Ben (solutions) will estimate costs and SOW line items.
- Helios: Alyssa (PM) — will own sample prompt set, procurement contact, and acceptance criteria.

Next steps (action items):
- Alyssa: confirm expected peak concurrent requests and provide your canonical prompt set (5–10 representative prompts).
- Redwood: deliver a concise capacity workbook + quote (attached XLSX) and the evaluation runbook (attached).
- Set kickoff: propose Tuesday (9/21) 10:00–11:00 PT for hands-on technical kickoff and test account provisioning.

Attachments: lighthouse-poc-capacity.xlsx (sizing + cost estimate), lighthouse-eval-plan.md (runbook).

Thanks — will be standing by to turn the POC on once we have your concurrency numbers and the prompt set.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni

Subject: Re: Recap & capacity proposal: Lighthouse POC (next steps + sizing)

Vivek — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side so your sizing aligns with what we'll run: 

- Typical daily active users for the pilot: ~120 (internal beta), expected peak concurrent RPS: around 16–20 (mostly short prompts, ~6–10 tokens generation on average).
- We consider average end-to-end latency of up to 5s acceptable for most calls; anything >10s is considered a failure for UI flows.
- Data residency: all PII must stay within our AWS us-west-2 region — we will provide the SSO and KMS contacts if needed.
- Security: we'll send over our completed security questionnaire (attached) and loop in our security lead (security-contact@heliossys.com). Procurement is cc'd to start SOW routing.

We can target the kickoff on 9/21 AM PT as you suggested. Please include a short slide deck in advance that outlines the test plan and the TTL for any test credentials. Also, please include a line item for a 30-minute post-POC readout.

I'll upload the representative prompts and a small test corpus by EOD 9/20.

Thanks,
Alyssa Monroe
Product Lead, Lighthouse | Helios Systems
alyssa.monroe@heliossys.com

On 9/19/27 5:04 PM, Alyssa Monroe wrote:
> Vivek — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side...

Thanks Alyssa — quick technical notes to justify the baseline + autoscale behavior so procurement has what they need: 

Sizing rationale:
- Baseline 4 GPUs: allows sustained concurrency of ~12–18 RPS for short-generation prompts when using continuous batching and a KV cache for repeated context. This assumes average prompt length and reply token counts similar to what you described.
- Burst to 8 GPUs: covers headroom for load-testing with synthetic traffic and short marketing-driven spikes. We'll enforce a 30–45 minute burst budget in config so costs are bounded.

Autoscale policy (proposed):
- Scale trigger: CPU/GPU utilization > 70% OR queue length > 40 requests for 2 consecutive minutes.
- Scale step: +2 GPUs per event.
- Cooldown: 3 minutes after scale-down to avoid flapping.
- Pre-warming: we can pre-warm an extra GPU for the scheduled campaign windows if you provide a 24-hour notice.

Cost / test quote (estimates):
- Baseline 4 x A100-equivalent: estimated $X,XXX/hr (Redwood internal rate used for POC quoting) — see attached XLSX for line items.
- Burst usage (per additional GPU/hr): $XXX/hr (we'll show incremental cost in the workbook).

Operational notes:
- We'll enable per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdowns for the trial so you can map quality vs. spend during your eval.
- For the POC, we recommend staying on a single model variant for quality comparison, then test a quantized variant only if cost-per-token needs lowering.

I'll be on the kickoff call 9/21 and will run the first smoke tests. Vivek / Ben will own commercial items and SOW.

Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
